title: Construct optimal reversible scratch schedules with replay certificates
body:
Fixed-lifetime allocators cannot choose recomputation or cleanup order. Add an exact reversible-pebble planner for small pure dependency DAGs, with different compute and erase costs and weighted scratch limits. The final state must contain exactly the requested outputs.

A separate checker verifies state closure and every edge-potential inequality, then replays the schedule literally to attain the lower bound. An unreachable goal has a finite closed-state certificate. The CLI binds the exact problem bytes and can check a saved certificate without shortest-path search.

Six tests pass normally and under -O on CPython3.12.14: all64 four-node DAGs at four budgets against independent set-state relaxation, the full16-node/65536-state limit, a weighted recomputation example, complete cleanup, impossible space limits, forged potentials/closure/costs and portable source-hash replay.

This is classical reversible pebbling and shortest-path certification. Limits:16 nodes; positive integer costs and widths at most10^12. Pure-node semantics, external input storage and legal compute/erase primitives are premises; native maps, dirty helpers, precision and complete charges remain separate. No kappa or frontier change. Fresh main/priorities/overlap checked at start and submission; canonical claim https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5776. All 6 new tests pass in the [hosted plan](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40383558996/job/121785823806) at this head. The plan fails on the unchanged assignment module (8 failures and 2 errors); replay is skipped. The existing fix is [PR #5761](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5761). Independent review remains pending.

Base: `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`. Verified head: `0ed431c52085852999a5817e80b508c1b3c63f75`.

Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Retained tool and mathematical predecessor credits apply. No selected-frontier change.
